root_cause: The tabbable utility's isHidden function incorrectly treats elements inside a display:none ancestor as non-tabbable when displayCheck is undefined (the default). The focus trap calls tabbable() without options, so displayCheck is undefined. The original code checks for display:none when displayCheck is falsy or 'full', causing the dialog's fields to be filtered out while the backdrop is still hidden (or during activation), so the focus trap finds no tabbable nodes and cannot move focus to #street.
repair_strategy: Modify isHidden in src/index.js to only perform the display:none ancestor walk when displayCheck === 'full'. When displayCheck is undefined (as called from the focus trap), skip the display:none check entirely, preserving only visibility:hidden and <details> closed checks. This allows the focus trap to see the dialog's fields as tabbable immediately after the backdrop becomes visible.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will now receive focus on the first input (#street) when opening the address dialog, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Considering elements with display:none as tabbable when displayCheck is undefined may cause unintended focus behavior in other contexts where tabbable is used on truly hidden elements; however, the component's usage is limited to the focus trap which ensures containers become visible before interaction, mitigating risk.
verification_requirements: After clicking the Add delivery address button, focus shifts to the #street input.
Typing an address and pressing Save updates the status accordingly.
Escape key closes dialog and returns focus to the button (regression guard).
The dialog remains accessible via screen readers (role dialog, aria-modal).
